stories.headline: India’s relation with ASEAN at heart of Act East Policy, says PM Modi
stories.deck: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Manila on November 16-17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr.
stories.bodyText:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 16, 2026) embarked on a visit to Manila in the Philippines to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on November 17, 2026. Mr. Modi is attending the summits at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
Ahead of his departure, Mr. Modi, in a statement, said, “Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India’s Act East Policy and occupies a central place in our MAHASAGAR vision. Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilizational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations.”
“At the ASEAN-India Summit, I look forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity,” he added.
Talking about The East Asia Summit, Mr. Modi said that it ‘provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges’.
“I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific,” the Prime Minister said.
Mr. Modi also said he looks forward to interacting with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines ‘whose contributions strengthen the bonds of friendship between our two countries’.
“I am confident that the visit will impart new energy to India’s partnership with ASEAN and reinforce our collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific,” he added.

stories.headline: U.S. govt seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun murder-for-hire plot
stories.deck: Gupta will be sentenced on November 20. His lawyers have, however, argued for a "substantial downward" sentence of 12 years' imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release
stories.bodyText:
The U.S. government is seeking a 24-year prison term for Indian national Nikhil Gupta, accused of being involved in a murder-for-hire plot against
Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun on American soil.
Gupta, 55, had pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with his efforts to murder Pannun in New York.
Gupta will be sentenced on November 20. His lawyers have, however, argued for a "substantial downward" sentence of 12 years' imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release.
Pannun holds dual American and Canadian citizenship.
In a 20-page submission to United States District Judge Victor Marrero at the Southern District of New York on Friday (November 14, 2026), United States Attorney James McDonald said Gupta’s “conduct was as brutal as it was brazen.
"He was a crucial participant in a foreign plot to execute a U.S. citizen on U.S. soil. The Court should impose a sentence that reflects the magnitude of the crime and sends a message that the violent silencing of voices in this country will not be tolerated. For these reasons, and all the reasons set forth above, the Government respectfully requests that the Court impose a sentence of 293 months’ imprisonment,” the U.S. government said.
They said that Gupta and his co-conspirators, “including at least one Indian Government employee”, plotted to kill an American citizen on U.S. soil because of the “victim’s political ideology.
“It is a crime of the utmost seriousness and demands an equally serious penalty... the Government submits that a sentence at the top of the United States Sentencing Guidelines range of 235 to 293 months’ incarceration is necessary to serve the legitimate purposes of sentencing.”
In his sentencing memorandum, Gupta asked that the Court impose a much reduced sentence.
Gupta’s lawyers have argued that the Probation Department calculated an advisory Guidelines range of “235 to 293” months imprisonment and has “recommended a substantial downward variance from that range to 144 months imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release."
"We join in Probation’s request for a significant downward variance from the Guidelines.”
Gupta’s lawyers have said that the probation’s recommendation reflects a considered judgment by the officer who interviewed Gupta, reviewed the full investigative record, and weighed the statutory factors.
“It takes into account that Gupta has no criminal history of any kind, that he was suffering from untreated alcohol dependence at the time of the offence, and that any lengthy sentence for a fifty-five-year-old man is significant,” his attorneys said, adding that Gupta “does not minimise” the seriousness of what he did.
“He agreed to arrange the murder of another person, and that conduct warrants a term of imprisonment. But the sentence this Court imposes should be sufficient, and not greater than necessary, to serve the purposes of sentencing as to this defendant,” Gupta’s lawyers said.
Gupta “pleaded guilty to a serious offence, and he does not minimise it. The Court must still sentence him as the whole person the record shows. He has no criminal history."
According to the allegations contained in the indictment, other public court documents, and statements made in court, in about 2023, Gupta worked together with others in India and elsewhere, including with co-defendant Vikash Yadav to plot Pannun’s assassination on U.S. soil.
"He acted under pressure from Yadav, a man he believed had the power of the Indian state behind him, while his untreated alcohol dependence clouded his judgment. He did not stand to gain from the payment that is the basis of all three counts. He has spent more than three years in custody, first in the Czech Republic and then at the Metropolitan Detention Centre, and he has the support of a family and community who will help him rebuild his life,” Gupta’s lawyers have said.
In a letter to the court, Gupta said he wishes he could “turn back time to 2023 and undo my mistakes,” and that when he looks back, “I don’t even recognise the man I had become.”
In the letter, Gupta describes how, in early 2023, he became distant from his family and began drinking heavily almost every night. Of his family and the people around him, he wrote: “I deeply regretted the suffering I caused them and the people around me.”
He has told the Court that he is “so thankful that my actions did not result in the loss of human life or injury,” which “would have been the greatest regret of my life.”
At Yadav’s direction, Gupta contacted an individual whom he believed to be a criminal associate, but who was in fact a confidential source working with the Drug Enforcement Administration for assistance in contracting a hitman to murder Pannun in New York City.
Yadav subsequently agreed, in dealings brokered by Gupta, to pay the undercover officer $100,000 to murder the Victim. On or about June 9, 2023, Yadav and Gupta arranged for an associate to deliver $15,000 in cash to the undercover officer as an advance payment for the murder.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang sets up 'war room' to comeback as Nvidia CEO: Report
stories.bodyText: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is eyeing a comeback into the position and has discussed a possibility of returning with his allies, Financial Times reported on Sunday. According to the report citing sources, Huang is setting up a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to advocate for his return and would try to garner support from the White House. "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," an ally told FT, adding that the efforts had Huang's support. .Jensen Huang carried a secret for more than a year, leading to his downfall. This comes after Nvidia's board had reportedly approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings' CEO Rene Haas as the successor to Huang. Huang stepped down as the CEO last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy, raising questions over exports of the company's advanced AI chips to China. There are reports of two more affairs with separate employees of Nvidia. The scandal has plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. (With Reuters inputs)

stories.headline: I want to win matches for India for a long time: Naman Dhir
stories.deck: In an exclusive conversation with TOI, Naman Dhir spoke about his rapid rise, the challenges of life in international cricket, his bowling transformation, and his dream of featuring in the 2027 ODI World Cup.
stories.bodyText:
MOUNT MAUNGANUI: For Naman Dhir, earning an India cap was never the finish line. The 26-year-old all-rounder believes his real journey has only just begun. In an exclusive conversation with TOI, Dhir spoke about his rapid rise, the challenges of life in international cricket, his bowling transformation, and his dream of featuring in the 2027 ODI World Cup.
ExcerptsHas the feeling of playing for India sunk in?
Everything happened at a rapid pace. It has now. The call-up itself came as a surprise. I had no idea I would be picked for the West Indies ODIs, so it took a couple of days to sink in. Once I joined the team, though, everything felt normal. I’m also happy that we managed to win both the ODI and T20I series in New Zealand. I was performing whenever opportunities came my way and had already played a few IPL seasons in flexible roles. I always believed the chance would come when the time was right.
Were there any hints during the Sher-E-Punjab T20, where Shubman Gill was also playing?
Not at all. It came completely out of the blue. I had just returned from the tournament and was unpacking my whites to prepare for the Ranji Trophy when I saw the squad announcement on Instagram.
Does it feel like mission accomplished?
Playing for India is every cricketer’s dream, but for me, the job is far from done. 
I want to play for a long time and win matches for India. I don’t set specific targets. My focus is on contributing to victories and remaining part of the team for as long as possible.
How much work have you put into your bowling?
I’ve always bowled, but my understanding improved significantly after joining 
Mumbai Indians
. Working with quality coaches and players, especially Rahul Sanghvi sir, helped me understand the craft much better. Over the last two to three years, I’ve increased my workload and made technical changes, including using my body and shoulder more effectively.
For an off-spinner in white-ball cricket, is it more about heart than skill?
You definitely need both. Modern white-ball cricket is demanding because almost any target feels chaseable. You have to be brave, but you also need a clear plan. It’s about knowing when to bowl a defensive delivery, when to concede a single, and when to attack for a wicket.
Do you remember walking into the Mumbai Indians dressing room for the first time?
Sharing a dressing room with players like Rohit Sharma, Hardik Pandya and Suryakumar Yadav felt surreal. For the first few days, I was hesitant, wondering how to approach them. But everyone made me feel welcome. I developed a very close bond with Hardik bhai. We discussed batting extensively, and those conversations helped me settle in quickly.
Is batting at No. 6 or 7 tougher than people realise?
Absolutely. It’s not just about walking in and swinging from ball one. But I enjoy the challenge. Honestly, I’m happy batting anywhere. Even openers have to attack these days. If you’re coming in around the 15th or 16th over, you usually get a few deliveries to assess conditions before looking to accelerate. If you stay calm and make smart decisions, the role becomes easier.
How has working with Gautam Gambhir been?
He’s very clear. He wants players to be switched on, make smart decisions and give everything on the field. Even if you score a hundred, you’ll get a pat on the back and then be challenged to do even better in the next game.
Do you still have red-ball ambitions?
Absolutely. Red-ball cricket will always remain a priority for me. Before the India call-up, I was preparing for the Ranji Trophy and had set myself the goal of scoring big runs. I believe that if you perform consistently in the longest format, every other format becomes easier.

Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
briefs.deck: A six-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate in a classroom in Panchkula, with CCTV footage capturing the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety, supervision, and the influence of violent video games on children
briefs.bodyText:
The school’s auto-rickshaw arrived at its usual time around noon on October 28. Homemaker Aarti (name changed to protect privacy) took a quick, reassuring look at her six-year-old daughter’s uniform and schoolbag before waving her off with a smile. However, at 3:30 p.m., when the auto-rickshaw driver went to pick her up from her school in Haryana’s Panchkula district, the girl was nowhere to be found. Her bag was kept at the school’s reception area.
The driver informed her family, who live just five minutes away from the school, and her father came rushing. As he called out her name, his voice grew louder with every frantic step towards the school building. He asked the teachers about his daughter’s whereabouts, and they joined him in his search. Soon, a boy approached him, asked his daughter’s name and confirmed whether he was looking for her. When the father nodded, the boy led him to a classroom on the first floor, telling him that someone had beaten her up.

briefs.deck: Incidentally, the Israeli delegation’s visit and the collaboration does not show up on the schedule of T-Hub, while the schedule is reported in tech-websites.
briefs.bodyText:
In a pre-dawn operation, the Mir Chowk police allegedly detained activists of the Students Islamic Organisation of India on Monday (November 16, 2026). In a statement at about 1 a.m., the SIO said: SIO Telangana leaders faced a late-night arrest for opposing an Israeli company’s event at T-Hub Hyderabad, amplifying the cause of Palestine. Silencing voices of conscience cannot deter a cause driven by conviction, courage & justice. Our solidarity with Palestine remains unwavering.”
On Monday (November 16, 2026), Hyderabad is scheduled to host a delegation of 20 Israeli companies at T-Hub, a technology incubator of Telangana state. According to the programme schedule, the event is set to create space for collaboration between the Israeli companies in the defence technology, data centre infrastructure, robotics, cybersecurity, semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI) sectors with Indian companies.
Earlier, on Saturday (November 14, 2026), some rights organisations and social activists addressed the media about their concerns about the collaboration between Israeli companies and Indian companies, as they alleged that the Israeli organisations are part of the defence and research development departments in Israel.

briefs.headline: Tripartite agreement signed for ₹1,000-crore desalination project in Odisha
briefs.deck: Eleven projects worth around ₹15,498 crore, identified as part of the collaboration with IFC, were granted in-principle were approval by State’s Empowered Committee on Infrastructure
briefs.bodyText:
The Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (IDCO), the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Odisha government’s Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Cell have signed a tripartite agreement for a desalination project at Gopalpur in Ganjam district, at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore.
Dubbed as the first-of-its-kind PPP project in the State, the project is expected to produce 100 MLD (million litres per day) of water for industries
Kamal Dorabawila, Manager, PPP Transaction Advisory Services (South Asia) at IFC, said the organisation’s entire team was focused on making Odisha a strategic hub for globally competitive investment opportunities.
At the 66th meeting of the Empowered Committee on Infrastructure for PPP Projects, held recently under the chairpersonship of Chief Secretary Anu Garg, it was emphasised that the ongoing collaboration with IFC should focus on developing a pipeline of viable PPP projects across sectors, including affordable urban housing and industrial infrastructure, as well as projects with significant social impact.
The committee granted in-principle approval to 11 projects worth approximately ₹15,498 crore, identified under the collaboration with IFC.
Additionally, five new projects with an estimated cost of ₹831.68 crore were approved. The committee also reviewed the status of 28 ongoing PPP projects with a combined estimated cost of ₹28,764.28 crore.

Mountaineer turns protector for 18 hyenas near Pakhi Pahar
briefs.deck: In Purulia, West Bengal, Joydeep Chakraborty has been diligently working to shift the negative narratives surrounding striped hyenas. Starting his field research in 2017, he engaged local communities to foster understanding and reduce harmful practices against these vital scavengers. His efforts have led to the discovery of 18 to 19 hyenas through camera traps, underscoring their presence and…
briefs.bodyText:
When a striped hyena killed a goat in a village near Pakhi Pahar in West Bengal’s Purulia district, the loss was not just an encounter with wildlife for the family. Goats are an important source of income for many households in the area. Some villagers chased and killed hyenas in retaliation when livestock went missing.
Mountaineer and researcher Joydeep Chakraborty realised that protecting the animals would require him to understand why people feared them. Instead of limiting his work to searching the hills for wildlife, he began visiting homes, speaking to families and explaining the role striped hyenas play in the local ecosystem.
Nearly nine years after he began his focused fieldwork, his community-based efforts have helped change how some villagers view the animal. Chakraborty estimated that around 18 to 19 striped hyenas now live in his study area near Pakhi Pahar.
According to a report by award-winning journalist Partho Burman for The Better India, Chakraborty’s effort began with a chance encounter with the animal's call on a winter night in January 2017.
The night that changed his relationship with the hills
Chakraborty had been visiting Pakhi Pahar for years as a mountaineer. On January 14, 2017, he was camping beneath a tree when he heard a strange, sharp call coming from the darkness. 
He initially could not identify the animal. He switched on his torch and tried to follow the sound, but the creature disappeared before he could see it clearly.
“That was the first time I heard a striped hyena in the wild,” he told Burman. “I was scared. But that sound stayed with me.” Curiosity led him to look for information about striped hyenas in India. He found that there was limited research, particularly on the species in eastern India. He also learnt about the threats it faced, including habitat loss, road accidents and killings linked to conflict with people.
The more he read, the more he wanted to understand whether the animal was still present in the forests around Pakhi Pahar. He returned in 2018 and began exploring the surrounding hills and forests more systematically. From March that year, he started walking through the terrain with a few tribal villagers who helped him look for signs of hyena activity.
From searching for footprints to earning villagers' trust
Image courtesy: Instagram/@deeptodeepc
The first clear sign of progress came on March 8, 2020, when Chakraborty found a striped hyena footprint after nearly two years of searching. The Covid-19 lockdown soon interrupted his fieldwork. But the relationships he had built with local residents continued to matter. By then, villagers had become familiar with his visits and some had started helping him with his work. In February 2022, he captured the first photograph of a striped hyena in the region using a hand camera. It provided visual confirmation of the animal's presence.
He also continued speaking to families about the species. He explained that striped hyenas are scavengers that feed on carcasses, helping remove dead animals from the environment. He discussed their ecological role and tried to address the belief that they were simply dangerous animals that needed to be killed.
The conversations gradually began to make a difference. Chakraborty considers 2022 an important turning point, as retaliatory killings in the area began to reduce significantly.
Camera traps reveal more hyenas
In November 2021, the pregnant female hyena he had been tracking gave birth to three cubs. Chakraborty later saw the cubs emerge from their den. In May 2022, he installed camera traps provided by Idea Wild near the hyena's lair. After a forest fire destroyed the first set, he returned and installed them again. He clarified that he used the cameras on private land and in areas around villages, rather than inside protected forest areas, because permission was required for installations in the latter.
The footage showed the mother and her cubs, along with eight to ten other hyenas. Further sightings over the following years added to the evidence of their presence. Based on his observations, Chakraborty estimates that 18 to 19 striped hyenas inhabit his study area today. This is his estimate, not an official population figure. The forest department has also said that a formal population survey of striped hyenas in Purulia is still pending.
Why protecting the hyena matters
Striped hyenas are scavengers, and their feeding habits help remove animal carcasses from the environment. But they face several threats, including shrinking habitats, road accidents and retaliatory killings.
The Wildlife Trust of India has also
documented
 human-hyena conflict in Purulia. In a separate conservation initiative carried out with the West Bengal Forest Department, the organisation has highlighted the importance of community awareness, field surveys and local participation in protecting the species. Its work underlines that reducing conflict requires understanding both wildlife behaviour and the concerns of residents.
Chakraborty continues his work as an independent researcher, with Dr Anindita Bhadra of IISER Kolkata serving as his research mentor. He is also seeking grants to support women who helped collect field data. His work has not yet produced an official population survey, and the estimate of 18 to 19 animals needs to be viewed in that context. 
But the change in the way some villagers respond to the hyenas is an important part of the effort.
For Chakraborty, the work has involved more than walking long distances through the hills. It has meant returning to the same villages, listening to families who have lost livestock and building enough trust for people to consider protecting an animal they once feared.

stories.headline: Southern states account for 50% of research papers, 56% of patent applications
stories.deck: Tamil Nadu has emerged as the top performer in patent applications and research publications among Indian states. Southern states, including Karnataka and Telangana, collectively account for nearly half of India's research publications. The recent report from NITI Aayog highlights the country's scientific advancements, improving its position in the Global Innovation Index. International…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU/NEW DELHI: Nearly half of India's research output and 56% of patents came from southern states. Tamil Nadu, individually, outperformed all other states and Union territories (UTs) in the country in terms of patent applications, research publications and the number of incubators in 2024-25, according to India's first science and technology scoreboard released recently by the govt think tank, NITI Aayog.
However, Maharashtra tops the list in terms of the number of deep-tech startups, while Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of higher education institutions in the country.
Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Keralam together produced nearly 1.1 lakh research publications, accounting for 48.6% of India's national total of more than 2.2 lakh publications. Their combined contribution to patent applications was even higher, at 35,309, or 56.1% of the national total of 62,934. Together, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka accounted for nearly 70% of the five states' research publications and almost 70% of their patent applications.
Besides showing India's steady progress in science & technology ecosystem that led the country's improvement in the Global Innovation Index from 81st in 2015 to 38th in 2026, the scoreboard shows nearly 30% of the country's research publications involve international collaboration with the United States emerging as the biggest collaborator for research publication followed by Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, China and South Korea.
The scoreboard — an interactive platform that provides an integrated view of the country’s science & technology landscape — has been designed to facilitate evidence-based policymaking and benchmarking across States/ UTs.
Prof Umesh V Waghmare, secretary, department of science and technology, said after the launch that the scoreboard adds a valuable state-level picture to the national evidence base on science and technology, and highlighted the role of State S&T councils and state universities in widening India’s research base. 
The publication data is sourced from Web of Science/InCites, while patent application figures are based on Clarivate’s Derwent World Patents Index (DWPI). These are the respective datasets used by NITI Aayog for its state-level comparisons.
Vivek Kumar Singh, senior adviser, NITI Aayog, said the scoreboard has been built to go beyond the volume of output and capture quality, impact and collaboration, so that states can identify expertise and areas for focused action. Going beyond the volume of output, the scoreboard presents indicators of research quality, impact, collaboration and open access across priority research areas and three sectors, namely Academia, Government R&D Labs and Industry.

stories.headline: Almost three decades on, 85-year-old disabled BDA site allottee awaits removal of encroachments in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 For 85-year-old SM Mallaiah, the battle to remove encroachments blocking access to the main road from his house has not ended even after 28 years.During this time, encroachments that were small sheds have now become a permanent multi-storey commercial building, rising higher than his own house.
The property was allocated to the state govt employee in 1987 in a newly formed Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA) layout on 4th A Main Road, 4th Block, Basaveshwarnagar. The 4th A Main Road, along which his house was located, was linked to Magadi Main Road, according to BDA’s layout plan.
After paying Rs 19,950, he was issued a possession certificate on Aug 8, 1988, which showed a road on its western boundary. He then built a house on the site, following which the “revenue site holders”, who had earlier occupied the land, allegedly encroached on the road and put up sheds, blocking his access. Mallaiah alleged they also cut his electricity connection and destroyed underground sewage pipes.
Mallaiah told 
TOI
 that BDA’s engineering section did not take any action to evict the trespassers.
While he got the property allocated when he was in his mid-40s, he spent decades knocking on the doors of courts, consumer forums and a redressal committee for a path less than 100 metres long to be reclaimed.
Till 2010, Mallaiah used to regularly follow up on the matter with BDA head office, but then his health started deteriorating, which eventually made him bedridden. 
Over the last decade, his 56-year-old son BM Paramesh has taken up the matter, visiting BDA’s engineering section regularly.
“Due to his disability and old age, he stopped personal visits almost a decade ago, but he still didn’t give up and used to send petitions through me to BDA officials. But the situation around our house has now become worse. In 2021, the encroachers started constructing over the road permanently,” Paramesh said.
In Oct this year, Paramesh got slight relief when the district consumer commission issued a non-bailable warrant against the BDA commissioner through the city police commissioner.
Paramesh believes that the family spent more than Rs 5 lakh over the decades on the case. During that time, he lost his mother.
Legal battle
Mallaiah’s fight for access to the road began in 1998, when Bangalore Urban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum ruled in his favour.
Mallaiah filed criminal complaints against encroachers while they resorted to counter-complaints against him and his family. While the complainant claimed BDA assured him it would restore the road as per a high court order, it took no steps. Alleging deficiency in service, he later approached the consumer forum seeking a direction to BDA to form the road, besides compensation.
In its defence, BDA argued that Mallaiah was not a consumer and the forum had no jurisdiction. It said the relief sought was in the nature of a mandatory injunction that could not be issued. It added that it had been prevented by court orders from clearing the road, as the high court had directed that the encroachers’ applications be considered by a screening committee.
The consumer forum noted that the screening committee had rejected the encroachers’ claims on March 31, 1997. With no impediment left, it said, BDA, which has a task force and demolition squad, “can have no more excuse for dithering.”
On June 16, 1998, the forum directed BDA to remove all obstructions and encroachments within four months and restore the road to its original condition. If BDA failed, it would have to pay him Rs 50 per day after four months until the obstruction was removed.
We will solve it: BDA
BDA officials told TOI that the authority would only file for a bail hearing, as it cannot appear in court without knowing the case. The authority would seek the next date and, in the meantime, go through the file to see the status. Though the commissioner through a non-bailable warrant was supposed to appear Friday, he did not appear. The case was adjourned to Dec 4.
Officials said they would approach the complainant and solve the issue.
BDA commissioner P Manivannan said that if required, he would personally appear before the court: “We are not aware of the details of the case as the summons arrived suddenly. It recently came to my notice, but only through other officials. 
If someone complains, necessary action has to be taken. Our legal department will take care of it.”
No action yet: Complainant’s son
During an open house meeting in April this year, Paramesh directly addressed his grievance to BDA chairman NA Haris. “Despite Mr Haris directing the zonal commissioner (west) to take immediate action and remove encroachments from the road, the engineering section said they wanted approval from the legal section. But till today nothing has happened,” he said.

stories.headline: Bengaluru Skydeck cost estimate rises to ₹800 crore from ₹500 crore
stories.bodyText:
With preparatory work gathering pace for the proposed 250-metre-high Bengaluru Skydeck, the project’s tentative cost estimate has risen to ₹800 crore from the initial estimate of ₹500 crore. The project, one of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s pet projects, is expected to move to the next stage, with the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) likely to invite Expressions of Interest (EoI) from prospective investors and developers in the coming two days.
The project, which received the Cabinet approval in August 2024 when Siddaramaiah was Chief Minister and Mr. Shivakumar was his deputy, was initially estimated to cost up to ₹500 crore. The estimate was subsequently revised to ₹600 crore. The Hindu has learnt that the latest BDA document puts the tentative broad-order cost at around ₹800 crore. Sources in the BDA, however, argued that this is only a preliminary estimate based on the initial concept and proposed facilities, and neither an approved estimate nor the final project cost. The final cost will depend on the tower’s design and height, built-up area, facilities, and technical requirements.
The project is proposed to be implemented through a public-private partnership (PPP), primarily under a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer (DBFOT) arrangement, or another suitable PPP structure.
The EoI is intended to assess prospective investors’ capacity and commercial interest, as well as the project’s technical and financial feasibility and possible revenue- and profit-sharing models, officials said, pointing out that participation in the EoI will not confer any right or assurance of being awarded the project. The developer or concessionaire will be selected later through a competitive Request for Qualification (RFQ) and Request for Proposal (RFP) process.
The BDA has appointed KPMG Advisory Services Private Limited as Transaction Advisor to assess the project’s feasibility, recommend the PPP structure, and identify potential investors.
The proposed skydeck is envisaged as more than an observation tower, with facilities including a glass-floor viewing area, Bengaluru Tourism and Visitor Centre and digital interactive experience centre, besides other facilities. The final mix of facilities will depend on the feasibility assessment and project design.
Under the proposed arrangement, the private investor or concessionaire is expected to mobilise the capital required for construction and operation, while the BDA will make the identified land available for the project. The BDA does not envisage making a direct capital investment towards construction at the present stage. The concession period, revenue-sharing arrangement, and allocation of risks are among the terms yet to be finalised.
Following the Cabinet approval, Mr. Shivakumar, who was then Bengaluru Development Minister, had explored several locations for the project, including sites near Baiyappanahalli, Hemmigepura and Jnanabharathi. These were, however, dropped due to feasibility issues. The BDA later considered a site near Kommaghatta, but land acquisition requirements and technical challenges posed hurdles.
The currently identified site is near S.M. Krishna Main Road, which is set to form part of the Bengaluru Business Corridor (BBC). It is also a few kilometres from the Challaghatta Metro station, providing connectivity to the proposed development.

briefs.headline: Volunteers back in parks for a weekend of cleaning, birding and botanical art in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The city’s green spaces saw volunteers turn up in numbers Sunday as 
TOI
’s #IamBengaluru – Volunteer for Parks initiative continued with activities across the city.
At Railway Layout Park, Youth for Seva (YFS) volunteers took up plogging and mapped litter hotspots, while at Railway Layout Upakara Park, YFS led a waste segregation and dry litter collection activity. At BDA 10th Block Park in Banashankari, Adamya Chetana Foundation organised a care and maintenance activity for native saplings.
In Yelahanka, Naturalist School conducted a lake biodiversity walk and survey at Rachenahalli Lake Park. At Hennur Lake, Team Social Spotlight (TSS) led a bird-watching activity, and at Richmond Town Park, TSS also organised a botanical art activity where participants engaged with plants through art. At Shantinagar Park Ground, Indian Ploggers Army led a special solid waste segregation and clean-up activity.
NA Haris, Shantinagar MLA and BDA chairman, said, “Keeping our surroundings clean is everyone’s responsibility, not just that of the govt. We must reduce waste at the source rather than generate garbage and expect someone else to clean it up. Residents, associations and NGOs are doing their bit, but those who dump waste irresponsibly must be identified and educated.”
The #IamBengaluru – Volunteer for Parks initiative, presented by Multigen in association with Kristu Jayanti University and supported by the GBA, encourages citizens to take ownership of their neighbourhood parks and contribute to a greener Bengaluru.
Navaneeth TS, 34, Electronics City Phase 1 resident, said, “The litter is everywhere, and the amount of it that goes to landfill bothers me a lot. So, I’m doing my part to bring change. This is only a first step, and it was the first event for many of the people here.”
Jennifer Abraham, Richmond Town resident and travel agent, added it’s important to hold people responsible.“This is my environment, and I want it clean. I’d like others to see what we’re doing and do it themselves, and stop throwing pamphlets,” she said.
Rima Kashyap, 84, Richmond Town resident, added
, “We put up dual dustbins around the park at our cost, so garbage goes in the right places. It’s our responsibility to keep our parks clean and healthy as GBA just plants and goes; daily upkeep is ours.”
Stuti, student, NPS Rajajinagar said#IamBengaluru is a wonderful way for young people to take responsibility for the spaces around them. “Today, it reminded me that even a small community effort can make a meaningful difference to our environment.”
Sriyaa, student, Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology, said,“We often come to parks to enjoy nature, but forget to think about the effort needed to keep them clean. Instead of simply noticing the problem, we can take the first step ourselves and by leading through action, encourage others to do the same.”
Abhishek SA, MBA student, Alliance University, said Bengaluru’s parks and lakes are an important part of what makes the city special. “The lake biodiversity walk and using iNaturalist to identify species made me look at nature more closely and appreciate how much life exists around us. Initiatives like #IamBengaluru can turn that awareness into collective responsibility for the city’s parks and lakes.”

briefs.headline: Driver assaulted in Bengaluru over Rs 2.1 lakh salary dispute; 3 arrested
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A 30-year-old water tanker driver was allegedly abducted and assaulted by his former employer and three others over a pending salary of Rs 2.1 lakh.
Mohan G, a resident of Anandapura, stated in his complaint on Nov 6 that he had been working with 
Srinivas
, owner of Sri Water Tank Service in BDA Layout, for around two and a half years. He was paid a monthly salary of Rs 30,000. However, Srinivas failed to pay him his wages for seven months, amounting to approximately Rs 2.1 lakh.
Mohan quit the job one and a half months ago and asked Srinivas to clear his pending salary. However, the latter refused to pay him and abused him when he demanded his dues, Mohan said.
On Nov 4, Mohan went to Srinivas’s home to ask about his salary, leading to an argument between the two. The following day, Srinivas and three other men arrived near Mohan’s home and allegedly attacked him with an iron rod and kicked him, leaving him unconscious.
They placed him in the rear seat of their car and drove to the Marathahalli railway gate area. The four men dragged him out of the car and dumped him on a heap of gravel. Srinivas allegedly removed Mohan’s trousers and kicked him in his private parts while two other men also assaulted him. They abandoned him and fled, the complainant said.
However, Mohan regained consciousness and managed to hire an autorickshaw and, with police assistance, reached a hospital, where he received treatment.
JB Nagar police arrested Srinivas (45) and two others.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru woman duped of Rs 8 lakh in Instagram gift scam
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A promised gift parcel from London cost a 46-year-old woman Rs 8 lakh after she responded to an Instagram advertisement. Fraudsters who contacted her on 
WhatsApp
 convinced her to pay the “delivery and customs clearance” charges, eventually extracting money from her, her son and two friends.
According to the complaint filed by 
Swathi
 (name changed), a resident of Kaval Byrasandra, the fraud began on Oct 27, when she clicked on an Instagram advertisement and was redirected to WhatsApp. A person contacted her using a Pakistani mobile number, +92 3433838036, and befriended her, claiming to work in London and promising to visit India and meet her. He later told her that he had sent her a gift parcel.
The fraudsters subsequently claimed that the parcel, containing valuable gifts including pound sterling (GBP), had arrived at an airport in India but was seized by customs officials. They initially demanded Rs 16,000 towards delivery and customs clearance, followed by further payments under various pretexts, assuring her that the parcel would be delivered once the charges were cleared. They also threatened her with trouble if she failed to pay.
The fraudsters used eight WhatsApp numbers with Pakistani, Philippine and Indian country codes to communicate with her and pressure her into making payments.
Swathi transferred Rs 6.6 lakh from one of her bank accounts and Rs 45,000 from another. She also transferred Rs 50,000 and Rs 20,000 from two of her son’s bank accounts. Additionally, Rs 8,000 each was transferred through the digital payment app accounts of two of her friends.
By Nov 11, the total amount transferred to bank accounts and UPI IDs provided by the fraudsters was just shy of Rs 8 lakh. Swathi told police that the fraudsters had also asked her to make payments through cheques.
After realising she had been cheated, Swathi approached East cybercrime police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act and Section 318 (cheating) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

briefs.headline: Angry at wife, man sets godowns ablaze; worker dies of suffocation in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Angry that his wife had left him and moved to her parents’ home following a domestic dispute, a 36-year-old man went on a spree of setting scrap godowns and shops ablaze at Attibele, Anekal and Jigani. His actions resulted in the death of a worker who was sleeping inside one of the scrap godowns, police investigations revealed.
The accused, 
Jeevan Raj
, a native of Denkanikottai in Tamil Nadu, had been living at Suddaguntepalya for the past few years and was engaged in the onion business. He had married around eight years ago and was living with his wife and children. However, frequent arguments reportedly strained their relationship. Following this, she left him and moved to her parents’ house.
Angered by this, Raj began visiting his in-laws’ home requesting his wife to return. As she refused, he started venting his frustration by setting fire to scrap and vegetable shops.
On Oct 22, he set fire to a scrap godown and a vegetable shop at Balluru village in Anekal. A labourer identified as 
Manikanta
, 26, sleeping in the scrap godown, died due to suffocation.
In the next few days, Raj set fire to scrap godowns at Anekal and Jigani. 
He would reportedly stand and watch the flames engulf the shops and even record videos of the fires on his mobile phone.
200 CCTV cameras scanned to crack case
Initially, the fires were believed to be accidental. However, the repeated incidents following a similar pattern raised suspicion among police that they were deliberate acts of arson.
Police examined footage from more than 200 CCTV cameras to identify the suspect. During the investigation, they spotted a man moving suspiciously near the scrap shops. Investigators tracked Raj, who would travel on a bike. He has been remanded in judicial custody on charges of murder.

briefs.headline: Grinding stone murder of 7: Bengaluru police probe stamp papers, thumb impressions in suspected Rs 2.5-cr property transfer
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: The murder of seven members of a family was allegedly part of a conspiracy by prime accused S Indushekhar alias Arjun Indushekhar, 52, to gain control of his wife’s family’s properties worth around Rs 2.5 crore.
In a significant development, police have learnt that he had procured stamp papers before the murders and allegedly obtained the thumb impressions of the deceased on them afterwards.
Indushekhar, who married 
Sunitha
 around two decades ago, allegedly held a grudge against her family over personal disputes and had his eyes on the property owned by his mother-in-law, Rupavathi.
After killing Sunitha, Rupavathi and his brothers-in-law and sisters-in-law, he allegedly pressed their thumb impressions on the stamp papers individually. “A few stamp papers are empty. We are verifying whether the thumb impressions were taken before or after the murders,” a senior police officer said.
The documents have been sent to experts to ascertain whether the impressions were obtained after the victims were killed. “We are also verifying whether Sunitha and Rupavathi were able to sign, based on their banking and PAN card documents,” the officer added.
During interrogation, Indushekhar reportedly told police that his wife frequently insulted him, picked fights over trivial issues and subjected him to mental harassment. 
He also claimed that her mother and brothers always supported her, and that their interference in his married life had fuelled his resentment towards the entire family.
Indushekhar had attempted to conceal the murders by telling relatives that his wife and mother-in-law had gone on a pilgrimage. He reportedly confessed to inviting his in-laws’ families separately for dinner, asking them to prepare the meal and killing them while they were eating. 
He allegedly believed that disposing of the bodies in a forest would ensure that nobody discovered the murders.
Meanwhile, his daughter has admitted to helping him, claiming that he had promised to transfer her grandmother’s property in her name. She is accused of assisting him in the killings, destruction of evidence and transportation of the bodies.
Investigators have also learnt that the daughter brought floor cleaners to remove bloodstains after the murders.
“Indushekhar’s custody will end in a couple of days. By then, we will complete the crime reconstruction and mahazar. If required, we will seek an extension of his police custody,” the officer said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru Tech Summit: IIIT-B to showcase research projects, startup innovations
briefs.bodyText:
The International Institute of Information Technology-Bangalore (IIIT-B) will showcase its research in artificial intelligence (AI), digital public infrastructure (DPI), healthcare, telecommunications and smart manufacturing at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, to be held from Tuesday to Thursday.
The institute will present a range of projects, from digital identity systems used by countries across the world to AI-based tools for healthcare monitoring, smart manufacturing, and autonomous vehicles. It will also highlight its work on AI skilling and technology startups.
The institute will showcase five digital public infrastructure initiatives — MOSIP, OpenG2P, CDPI, COSS and INJI — which together support over 45 countries.
MOSIP helps countries build national digital identity systems and is being rolled out in more than 30 countries. OpenG2P helps governments provide welfare benefits, while CDPI and COSS support countries in developing digital public infrastructure. INJI provides an open-source platform to issue, store and verify digital credentials, the institution said.
Research in healthcare will include projects developed by the institute’s Electronics and Health Research Centre (EHRC), covering public health, surgery, assistive and rehabilitation devices, self-care tools and Tele-MANAS.
Among the projects on display will be a set of AI-based tools for remote health monitoring. These include a project aimed to predict the risk of sepsis at an early stage, FatigueShield, which forecasts fatigue and heat-stress risks and ArogyaSense, which helps identify the most clinically relevant information from health data, besides other projects.
IIIT-B COMET Foundation will showcase a prototype of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), a technology that uses electronically controlled surfaces to direct wireless signals, reduce interference and improve network coverage, particularly indoors and in private 5G networks. The project was developed with support from the institute’s Technology Innovation Hub under the Department of Science and Technology’s NM-ICPS programme.
The Karnataka AI Hub, supported by the State government and anchored at IIIT-B, will showcase its initiatives to build AI capabilities among students, professionals, researchers and entrepreneurs, while the institute’s Web Science Lab will present AnumatiDPI, a consent management platform that allows individuals and organisations to control access to and sharing of their data.

briefs.deck: According to the NIA, Pudumadam Imran was actively involved in a conspiracy to traffic Sri Lankan nationals by promising to facilitate their migration to Canada using valid documents
briefs.bodyText:
: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Friday (November 13, 2026) arrested Pudumadam Imran, an absconding accused in the Sri Lankan human trafficking case, after he was deported from Sri Lanka and handed over to Indian authorities.
Mr. Imran was detained by Sri Lankan authorities based on an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of the NIA. Following his repatriation to India, an NIA team arrested him at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru on November 13.
According to the NIA, Mr. Imran was actively involved in a conspiracy to traffic Sri Lankan nationals by promising to facilitate their migration to Canada using valid documents.
He allegedly collected money from the victims’ family members and relatives and transferred the funds through hawala channels to co-accused persons in India to facilitate the trafficking and illegal confinement of the victims.
The case originated in 2021 when local police conducted raids at premises in Mangaluru based on credible information and found several Sri Lankan nationals staying there without valid documents.
A case was registered in this connection under Crime No. 103/2021, invoking various sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Foreigners Act and the Passport Act.
The NIA subsequently took over the investigation and re-registered the case in July 2021 under Sections 120B (criminal conspiracy), 370 (trafficking of persons) and 420 (cheating) of the IPC, Section 14 of the Foreigners Act and Section 12(1A) of the Passport Act.
Earlier, two other accused who were absconding in the case, Seeni Aabul Khan (A-9) and Imran Khan (A-7), were arrested in 2024 and 2025, respectively. Both are currently facing trial before the Special Court for NIA Cases in Bengaluru.

stories.headline: Oil prices fall as surplus fears return after nine-month dry spell in the market
stories.deck: Oil prices are on a downward trend due to an anticipated surplus and a recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The International Energy Agency has indicated that supply could outstrip demand in the upcoming quarter, altering market forecasts. However, the United States has tightened restrictions on oil transport between its ports, complicating shipping logistics, while high freight…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices fell on Monday as concerns over a potential supply surplus weighed on the market, with shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovering to nearly pre-war levels after months of disruption. The US has also eased restrictions on transporting fuel between its ports, adding to expectations of higher supply.
WTI crude futures were trading at $88.35, down 21 cents or 0.24%, while Brent crude futures stood at $95.40, lower by 44 cents or 0.46%.
The market is increasingly factoring in the possibility that available supplies could exceed demand in the coming months. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday that the global oil market is expected to move into a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, reversing its earlier forecast of a supply deficit.
According to the agency, average oil supply during the quarter could reach 105 million barrels per day, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million barrels per day. The recovery in Middle East exports is expected to outpace growth in global demand, even as attacks on shipping continue.
"For the first time since the US-Iran conflict began, traders are actively contemplating the possibility of excess supply rather than persistent tightness. 
That shift in narrative is clearly dampening the tone," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.
The IEA also said 71 million barrels from the record release of emergency oil reserves pledged by its members in March would be made available by the end of February. This includes 15 million barrels of diesel intended to ease tightness in the market.
The downward movement in prices comes after both major benchmarks had already recorded steep weekly losses. Oil settled lower on Friday as traders assessed signs of reduced geopolitical risks from the US-Israeli war against Iran, now in its ninth month. WTI and Brent had shed 16% and 13%, respectively, over the previous week.
Another factor weighing on crude prices is the US decision to extend the suspension of restrictions under the Jones Act for another 90 days.
US President Donald Trump extended the waiver, a White House official said on Friday. The law normally requires cargo moved between US ports to be carried by US-flagged vessels. Its suspension allows foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and fuels, including petrol and diesel, between domestic ports, expanding the pool of available tankers.
However, the easing of supply concerns does not mean lower shipping costs. Waterer said that elevated freight rates were continuing to support oil prices.
The cost of transporting crude remains high because tankers face risks while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Vessel availability has also been affected by ships being tied up in transporting oil through the waterway, where cargoes are transferred to other vessels for onward delivery to refineries.
The risks to shipping were highlighted again on Sunday night, when Iran's navy said an oil tanker had caught fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media.

stories.headline: US flight chaos continues: 2,400 flights cancelled, 8,800 delayed as recovery drags on
stories.deck: US airlines faced significant disruptions as more than 10,000 flights were canceled or delayed due to technical failures. The issues resulted from maintenance work on routers used by the Federal Aviation Administration, leading to widespread communication problems. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the situation could normalize by Monday, highlighting ongoing challenges with aging…
stories.bodyText:
US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third day in a row.
While airlines raced to get their schedules back on track, transportation secretary Sean Duffy said that things could return to normal by Monday (local time).
The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is yet to identify the exact cause, even as the incident has renewed concerns about ageing technology and the need to upgrade the country's air traffic systems.
The disruption continued to affect airlines across the country on Sunday. According to aviation data site FlightAware, more than 2,300 flights were cancelled and around 7,700 delayed.
Saturday was even worse, with airlines cancelling more than 6,400 flights and reporting over 8,000 delays, according to Reuters.
JetBlue saw the highest cancellations on Sunday, with 28% of its flights affected. American Airlines cancelled 17% of its flights, while United Airlines, Southwest and Delta reported cancellations of 3% to 5%.
Speaking on ABC, Duffy said that flights would come "back to normal" on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday. 
He also stressed that keeping passengers safe remained the FAA's priority.
One router, a chain of problems: What went wrong
The trouble started with maintenance work involving routers used by the FAA. According to officials, the installation of at least one new router by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility led to a huge flow of data at other air traffic control centres, affecting their communication systems.
Duffy said the replacement of a router at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas. The Amarillo router began broadcasting, causing other routers at air traffic control centres across the country to become overloaded.
The FAA said on Sunday that it had disabled the "functionality of the originating routers". It also took the same step for around 60 similar routers used in the air traffic control system.
However, the exact reason behind the failure remains unclear. Duffy said the maintenance work had been carried out thousands of times in the past without any problems.
The worker who installed the router was not suspected of deliberately causing the disruption.
The worker was "a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran — so we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install," Duffy said. "But we don't actually have the root cause."
Duffy also said the routers that experienced problems were bought in 2001 and had become outdated by 2006.
FAA still has no clear answer
The technical failure led the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop on Friday, bringing nearly all departing flights to a halt for almost five hours.
It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks on the United States.
Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or any other deliberate attempt to disrupt the system. However, the FAA is still trying to establish what caused the failure.
The incident has once again highlighted the challenges facing the US air traffic control system. It has been struggling with ageing technology, equipment and communication problems, along with a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.
The flight disruptions have added urgency to the debate over modernising the country's air traffic control system.
Duffy has called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure, raising his earlier demand of $30 billion. This is in addition to the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year.
US President Donald Trump also called for more funding on Sunday, making his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions.
"We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," Trump wrote on social media. "Congress must approve."
But the demand for more money has not gone unchallenged. US Representatives Rick Larsen and André Carson, the top Democrats on the House of Representatives Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and its aviation subcommittee, respectively, questioned why additional funds were needed.

stories.headline: Equity vs bonds
stories.deck: Concentrated bets in equity market could generate high returns if your bet turns right; On the other hand, diversification pays off for bond investments
stories.bodyText:
Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.
In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.
